transitions.description: Stop request or open guard overrides all other inputs and clears the latch.
Permitted start sets the run command.
Permitted start while running keeps the run command set.
Retain run when no stop, open guard, or start command is present.
Retain cleared state when no stop, open guard, or start command is present.

timer_plan.notes: No timers or timer function blocks are required. All behavior is scan-level retained logic with same-scan safety override.

priorities: 1. Stop = TRUE forces Run = FALSE regardless of Start or GuardClosed.
2. GuardClosed = FALSE forces Run = FALSE regardless of Start or Stop.
3. If not overridden, Start = TRUE and GuardClosed = TRUE sets Run = TRUE.
4. If no override and no Start request, retain the previous Run state.
5. Safety/reset conditions are evaluated before start/retention, so open guard and Stop override Start in the same scan.
scan_execution_order: 1. Edge sampling: sample Start, Stop, and GuardClosed once per scan; capture retained pre-state RunPrev := Run. No edge detection is required because inputs are level-sensitive.
2. Safety/reset priority & state transitions: if Stop OR NOT GuardClosed then nextRun := FALSE; else if Start then nextRun := TRUE; else nextRun := RunPrev. Execute exactly one transition per scan.
3. Unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF: none; no timer function blocks are used.
4. Unified output assignments: Run := nextRun; update RunPrev := Run for the next scan. No output assignment occurs outside this stage.
